newsitem.title: QATAR: Gulf Arabs to try and resolve Qatar-Baharain row.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Arabs to try and resolve Qatar-Baharain row.

text.p: Gulf Arab states have agreed to form a three-nation committee to try and resolve a Bahraini-Qatari territorial dispute over an area potentially rich in oil and gas, officials said on Sunday.
"The committee will be chaired by Saudi Arabia with the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait as members," said one senior official attending the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) summit.
Bahrain boycotted the annual December 7-9 summit because of the dispute with host Qatar which has denied charges of spying against two of its citizens standing trial in Bahrain.
"The charges are fabricated," said Qatar's Foreign Minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim al-Jabr al-Thani in a television interview. "GGC sessions are not boycotted," he added.
Some diplomats say that tests had shown that the disputed area did not contain large reserves.

The cluster of Gulf islands and sandbanks have been held by Bahrain since the 1930s. In 1990 the two tiny states agreed to seek Saudi Arabian mediation for six months and to refer the issue to the International Court of Justice if a solution was not found.
Bahrain later said the dispute should be solved within a GCC context and has demanded Qatar withdraw its case from the world court.
Bahrain's boycott of the summit has angered the other GCC states, which also include Oman.
Qatar boycotted the final session at last year's GCC summit in Muscat but Bahrain's outright boycott was the first since the political and economic alliance was formed in 1981.
